description: Fixed 40-question synthetic eval corpus for the reader. Human-authored expected facts, source locators and completeness annotations. No real credentials, no customer content, no host paths.
scoring_rules: An answerable item is correct only when every entry of expected_claims is stated by a published claim unit that carries a citation which mechanically verifies and whose locator contains that claim's locator (its own `locator`, or the item's expected_locator when it declares none). A claim unit is the assertion text attached to one run of rendered [cN] markers, so a value is credited only against the evidence the same assertion carries.

An expected_claims entry is stated when one clause of a unit names the subject (or a subject_alternative), names the value (or an alternative), carries no negation between the two, and asserts no competing value of the declared value_type. This replaces raw substring matching over expected_facts, which accepted a negation of the fact and a different value in the same sentence: for max_retries = 3, "max_retries is not 3 but 4" contains "3" and scored correct.

expected_facts is retained, unchanged, as the diagnostic breakdown a failing run is attributed with (FACTS_MISSING / LOCATOR_MISMATCH). It no longer decides correctness for any item that declares expected_claims, which every answerable item here does.

A published quote under the general 8-byte support floor may still support a short expected quote when it comes from the one citation whose locator exactly equals the expected locator and the quote exactly equals the expected quote; a short quote from any other locator, or one that only partially matches, does not.
A no-answer item is correct only when the answer asserts nothing about the missing fact; a refusal on an answerable item scores zero and cannot offset it.
Citation semantic support is judged against the human-authored expected quote, not against the model's own claim.
Any leaked source region outside a published quote, any invalid published citation, any wrong model, and any cap breach fail the whole gate regardless of the averages.
